The concentration of P in the solution needs to be finely balanced – high enough to prevent desorption but low enough to hinder further adsorption by the soil.
This delicate equilibrium is disrupted when soils are subjected to flooding, a phenomenon observed across various soil types in the mid to long term.
This observation underscores the tendency for adsorption properties to converge, irrespective of soil type or location.
